quarterly_data.signal: CEO Paulo Ruiz, FY2026 guidance raised: 'we now expect total organic growth to be between 11% and 13%, up 200 basis points at the midpoint from the prior 9%-11% range', driven by Electrical Americas 'up 200 basis points to a midpoint of 15% growth, and Electrical Global up 450 basis points to a midpoint of 12% growth'; 'we expect full-year EPS to be between $13.40 and $13.60, $13.50 at the midpoint' (adjusted EPS midpoint raised by $0.22); segment margin guidance ranges and cash flow expectations reaffirmed; Q3 guidance provided in the presentation. CEO on the progression: 'We started the year saying we'll grow 8%, and the last earnings call we said we'd grow 10%, now we said 12%. The same is true for Americas, right? We started, I think it was 10%, then 13%, and now it's 15%.' On the implied second-half Electrical Global slowdown: 'We are very prudent here ... There's no downside here.' The Q2 IEEPA refund impact was less than $3 million ('$2.8, if you want to be precise'), less than $0.01 of EPS.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic growth 11%-13% (from 9%-11%); adjusted EPS $13.40-$13.60; Electrical Americas 15% and Electrical Global 12% at midpoint

quarterly_data.signal: Orders and backlog (call): CFO Dave Foster — for the combined electrical segments, on a rolling 12-month basis 'orders accelerated up 38%, and our book-to-bill ratio for our electrical sector was 1.2. Our backlog for our total electrical business increased 43% over prior year'; Electrical Global orders up 33% on a rolling 12-month basis; Aerospace 'robust orders driving backlog expansion and book-to-bill increasing to 1.2'. CEO Paulo Ruiz — Electrical Global total backlog 'is up 103%' including Boyd; Electrical Americas backlog grew 'another $700 million' sequentially even as organic growth accelerated to 18%. Outside data centers: 'Our total electrical orders increased mid to high teens for commercial, institutional, utility, industrial, and even residential'; machine OEM 'rebounded even faster with orders in the mid-30s'.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrical orders +38% R12M, book-to-bill 1.2, backlog +43% YoY; Electrical Global orders +33%, backlog +103%; Americas backlog +$700M QoQ

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 segment detail (call): CFO Dave Foster — acquisitions added seven points of growth and 'Each acquisition is at or above our expectations for growth and margins'; first-half adjusted EPS $5.96, a first-half record; the $0.25 segment profit beat versus guidance was partially offset by $0.15 from a higher tax rate. Combined electrical: organic growth 18%, total growth 27%, segment margins 24.5%, 110 basis points higher than Q1. Electrical Americas: growth also from machine OEM and commercial and institutional; the majority of the year-over-year margin decline was 'driven by temporary negative price cost', and with pricing actions in Q2 and early Q3 it should 'return to a roughly neutral impact in the second half'. Electrical Global: total growth 44% (organic 18% from data center, utility and machine OEM, plus 25% from Boyd); operating margin 19.8%, down 30 basis points from prior year but 'about a point higher than I had expected'; the planned general price increase was pulled in from Q4 to Q3. CEO Paulo Ruiz — in Electrical Global, revenues were up 20% in both EMEA and APAC; machine OEM up more than 20%, utilities and commercial / institutional up low teens; the EMEA turnaround in the last 18 months is 'really remarkable'. Aerospace (CFO): organic growth 7%, record quarterly sales and Q2 record segment profit on commercial OEM and aftermarket; Ultra PCS added six points of growth and is accretive; operating margin up 60 basis points to 22.8%. Mobility: down 2% organically, fully offset by foreign exchange; slightly positive excluding the intentional exit of a low-margin business; margins up 90 basis points year over year.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrical organic 18%, total 27%, margin 24.5%; Electrical Global margin 19.8%; Aerospace organic 7%, margin 22.8%; H1 adjusted EPS $5.96

quarterly_data.signal: Electrical Americas margin walk (CFO Dave Foster): Q1 to Q2 'up almost 190 basis points. About 100 points of that was price cost, and the other 90 points was pure output'; H1 to H2 up 450 to 500 basis points, 'All of our pricing actions have either been implemented in Q2 or early August'; 'Q2 to Q3, which is a 250 basis point improvement, 150 basis points is price cost and 100 basis points is output and productivity'; Q3 to Q4 'a 200-250 basis point improvement. 150 basis points is price cost and 50-100 is output and productivity'. Drivers: regular time instead of overtime and less premium cost, more experienced operators, manufacturing-engineering cost-out, then productivity investments in capital spending; discrete as well as general price increases. 'I have early reads on July as of this morning. It's an improvement from what we saw in second quarter. I'm feeling very confident about our exit rate for 2026.' CEO Paulo Ruiz: the bulk of the ramp disruption happened in 'Q4 last year and Q1 this year', and 'the expansions are going well and progressing better than planned now in Q2.'
quarterly_data.figure: Americas margin +250bps Q2-Q3 and +200-250bps Q3-Q4; Q1-Q2 almost +190bps (about 100 price cost, 90 output)

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and lead times (call): CEO Paulo Ruiz — revenue per day 'up 16% in a year'; 'we cleared the biggest hurdle we had in terms of sequential order, revenue per day growth, which was the sequential Q1 to Q2'. On lead times: 'we believe we can and should improve, and we know the product lines where our lead times are extended. We are ramping capacity not only in the factories, but we're ramping engineering support, and we're going to knock them down'; plants are delivering better volume and output and 'Top line should grow faster with less bottlenecks.'
quarterly_data.figure: revenue per day +16% in a year; lead times extended on some product lines

quarterly_data.signal: Markets and portfolio (call, CEO Paulo Ruiz): 'we estimate our total addressable market will grow about 10% this year'; expectation for the machine OEM market raised to solid growth. Outside data centers, Q2 organic revenue was double-digit in commercial and institutional, machine OEM and distributed IT. Scale: it took 112 years to reach $20 billion of revenue and the following decade added $1 billion; 'beginning of 2024 to end of 2026, including our renewed guidance, we will add $10 billion to the top line'. Portfolio: acquired Fibrebond (data-center modular builds), Resilient Power ('the medium-voltage solid-state transformers for 800 volt DC'), Boyd and Ultra PCS (defense systems) — 'Now we can actually say we have the complete portfolio going from the utility all the way down to the chip' — and is separating Mobility 'to move away from the automotive sector'; go-to-market has moved to a hybrid model of strong distribution and strong direct accounts. Boyd integration is 'going really well', and 'the strategic importance to have a seat on the table with the chip manufacturers ... will bring benefits to our power, also our software business'. Fibrebond is being scaled up; in white space with 800-volt DC 'we can also tap on their capability and also cut other partnerships to win in that space.'
quarterly_data.figure: TAM growth about 10% this year; $10 billion to be added to the top line from beginning of 2024 to end of 2026, including guidance
